Attributed Notes

Record what a counterpart said about themselves in panels, each line timestamped and marked as their words, with unverified figures rendered in grain.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1PanelElevated card, one topic a panel; panels sit in an auto-fit grid of 18rem columnselevated, border
2HeadTopic in mono caps (h3), and the source line: His words, unverifiedtext, text-secondary
3LineA bold lead phrase, then the note in their wordstext, text-secondary
4TimestampWhere in the transcript, right aligned from a 22rem paneltext-secondary, tabular figures
5Unverified figure37 grain on the line: a number they gave that nobody checkednone

Usage

Use it when

  • Background a counterpart gave about themselves, kept apart from what was checked.
  • A recap where attribution matters: who said it, when.

Do not use it when

  • Do not put a sensitive personal fact in a note, even in their words; leave it out of the page.
  • Do not present an unverified figure in sharp type.
  • Do not mix the author's reading into a panel; that is 57 Ledger row.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
panels[]{title, source, lines[]}yeslines[] are {lead, text, at, unverified?}.

Access

  • Each panel is a heading and a list, so a screen reader announces the topic and the count.
  • Unverified is said in words in the source line and in the text; grain repeats it.
